title: From GAN-Based Models to GPT-5: A Taxonomy-Guided Study of Human Performance in Detecting Deepfake Face Images
title_zh: 【输入内容第一行】的中文翻译：从基于GAN的模型到GPT-5：分类学指导下的深度伪造人脸图像人类检测能力研究

paragraphs.en: 该研究提出深度伪造人脸伪影分类体系DFAT，通过大规模实验揭示人类检测能力因生成模型而异，且模型专项训练比通用训练更能提升检测效果。 Generative models for deepfakes have rapidly evolved from GAN-based architectures to diffusion models and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, empirical research on human performance in detecting deepfake face images has not kept pace. It remains unclear if (and how) detection performance varies across generative models and whether model-specific training improves detection more effectively than general-purpose training. In this paper, we propose the \emph{Deepfake Face Artifact Taxonomy} (DFAT), a cross-model taxonomy of human-recognizable visual artifacts in deepfake face images, based on which we build both general-purpose and model-specific training materials. Through an online experiment ($n = 524$), we examined human performance in detecting deepfake face images and evaluated training efficacy across five representative generative models: three GAN-based, one diffusion-based, and one MLLM (GPT-5). Our results show that participants' detection accuracy was strongly model-dependent and that images generated by more recent and advanced models were not necessarily harder to detect. After training, participants achieved significant performance gains across most conditions, and their improvement varied by model. Notably, model-specific training generally yielded greater numerical gains than general-purpose training. In a five-month follow-up test ($n = 342$), we observed no significant decline in detection accuracy and no significant increase in perceived stress. Overall, our findings provide actionable insights for designing effective, sustainable, and targeted training programs to counter the growing threat posed by deepfakes.
paragraphs.zh: 生成式模型（generative models）用于生成深度伪造内容，已从基于GAN的架构快速演进到扩散模型和多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）。 然而，关于人类检测深度伪造人脸图像表现的实证研究却未能跟上这一步伐。 目前仍不清楚检测表现在不同生成模型之间是否存在差异（以及如何差异），也不清楚模型专项训练是否比通用训练更能有效提升检测效果。 在本文中，我们提出了\emph{深度伪造人脸伪影分类体系}（Deepfake Face Artifact Taxonomy, DFAT），这是一个针对深度伪造人脸图像中人类可识别视觉伪影的跨模型分类体系，并基于此构建了通用训练材料和模型专项训练材料。 通过一项在线实验（$n = 524$），我们考察了人类检测深度伪造人脸图像的表现，并评估了跨五个代表性生成模型的训练效果：三个基于GAN的模型、一个基于扩散的模型和一个多模态大语言模型（GPT-5）。 我们的结果表明，参与者的检测准确率高度依赖于具体模型，且由更新、更先进的模型生成的图像并不一定更难检测。 训练后，参与者在大多数条件下都取得了显著的性能提升，且其提升幅度因模型而异。 值得注意的是，模型专项训练总体上比通用训练带来了更大的数值提升。 在一项为期五个月的随访测试（$n = 342$）中，我们观察到检测准确率没有显著下降，感知压力也没有显著增加。 总体而言，我们的发现为设计有效、可持续且有针对性的训练方案以应对深度伪造日益增长的威胁提供了可操作的洞见。
